units.source:
This chapter describes what happens between the English source and the
translated pages you can read in the other languages.

The author edits only the English `.qmd` files and `_quarto.yml`. Each
translated language lives in a set of translation files under `_i18n/`, one
file per chapter. Every paragraph, caption and code comment is a separate unit
with its own source text, translation and list of reviewers.

Running `i18n translate` collects the units that are new or whose English text
has changed. A translator fills them in, and the tool checks every result
before it is accepted. Inline code, links, citations, cross-references and
shortcodes must come back unchanged, and translated code must parse with R's
own parser.

When a paragraph changes in English, its translation becomes *stale*. Readers
then see the English paragraph, marked as such, until the unit is translated
again. A translation is never silently wrong.

In code cells, only comments and display strings such as plot titles are
translated. Variable names and data never change, so every language runs the
same analysis. If a translated cell fails, the build uses the English cell.

Choose **Review this page** in the notice to turn on reviewer mode. Each
paragraph is marked by the number of people who have reviewed it. Select a
paragraph to see the English source, then approve the translation or suggest
a better one. Your changes are collected and submitted together as a pull
request.

This demo uses a local mock of the pull request service. It runs the same
checks as the real service and saves each pull request on disk instead of
opening it on GitHub.
